 // NULL deref here!\\n    if(num > klen) {\\n      memcpy(buf, global_passwd, klen + 1);\\n      return klen;\\n    }\\n  }\\n  return 0;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**What was wrong**: If `global_passwd` was NULL (user didn't provide a password), calling `strlen((char *)global_passwd)` would crash with a NULL pointer dereference.\\n\\n**The Fix**:\\n```c\\nstatic int passwd_callback(char *buf, int num, int encrypting,\\n                           void *password)\\n{\\n  DEBUGASSERT(0 == encrypting);\\n  \\n  if(!encrypting && num >= 0 && password) {  // Added NULL check!\\n    int klen = curlx_uztosi(strlen((char *)password));\\n    if(num > klen) {\\n      memcpy(buf, password, klen + 1);\\n      return klen;\\n    }\\n  }\\n  return 0; This is a **cross-domain cookie leakage vulnerability**.\\n\\n**Buggy Code**:\\n```c\\nstatic bool tailmatch(const char *little, const char *bigone)\\n{\\n  size_t littlelen = strlen(little);\\n  size_t biglen = strlen(bigone);\\n  \\n  if(littlelen > biglen)\\n    return FALSE;\\n  \\n  return Curl_raw_equal(little, bigone+biglen-littlelen) ? So:\\n- Cookie domain: `example.com`\\n- Would match: `bexample.com` ❌ (WRONG!)\\n- Should only match: `.example.com`, `www.example.com` ✓\\n\\n**The Fix**:\\n```c\\nstatic bool tailmatch(const char *cooke_domain, const char *hostname)\\n{\\n  size_t cookie_domain_len = strlen(cooke_domain);\\n  size_t hostname_len = strlen(hostname);\\n  \\n  if(hostname_len < cookie_domain_len)\\n    return FALSE;\\n  \\n  if(!Curl_raw_equal(cooke_domain, hostname+hostname_len-cookie_domain_len))\\n    return FALSE;\\n  \\n  /* RFC6265 4.1.2.3: cookie domain must match exactly OR \\n     be preceded by a dot for subdomain matching */\\n  if(hostname_len == cookie_domain_len)\\n    return TRUE;  // Exact match\\n  if('.' == *(hostname + hostname_len - cookie_domain_len - 1))\\n    return TRUE;  // Proper subdomain with dot\\n  return FALSE;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Impact**: Cookies could leak across different domains, allowing unintended cookie sharing and potential security breaches.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 3. **base64 encoding/decoding bounds checks in lib/base64.c**\\n\\n**CVE**: CVE-2016-8617 - [Commit efd24d5](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/efd24d57426bd77c9b5860e6b297904703750412) - \\\"base64: check for integer overflow on large input\\\" (September 27, 2016)\\n\\n**The Bug**:\\nOn 32-bit systems, very large input to base64 encoding could cause **integer overflow** when calculating the output buffer size.\\n\\n**Buggy Code**:\\n```c\\nstatic CURLcode base64_encode(const char *table64,\\n                              struct Curl_easy *data,\\n                              const char *inputbuff, size_t insize,\\n                              char **outptr, size_t *outlen)\\n{\\n  if(!insize)\\n    insize = strlen(indata);\\n  \\n  base64data = output = malloc(insize * 4 / 3 + 4); This wasn't necessarily a security bug but a **robustness/denial-of-service issue**.\\n\\n**What was wrong**: \\nThe old `Curl_conn_shutdown_blocking()` function would block indefinitely waiting for proper connection shutdown:\\n\\n```c\\nCURLcode Curl_conn_shutdown_blocking(struct Curl_easy *data, int sockindex)\\n{\\n  // ... \\n  while(cf) {\\n    while(!done && !result) {\\n      result = This is a **cross-domain cookie leakage vulnerability**.\\n\\n**Buggy Code**:\\n```c\\nstatic bool tailmatch(const char *little, const char *bigone)\\n{\\n  size_t littlelen = strlen(little);\\n  size_t biglen = strlen(bigone);\\n  \\n  if(littlelen > biglen)\\n    return FALSE;\\n  \\n  return Curl_raw_equal(little, bigone+biglen-littlelen) ? TRUE : FALSE;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**What was wrong**: The function only checked if the cookie domain was a **suffix** of the hostname, but didn't verify there was a proper domain boundary (a dot). So:\\n- Cookie domain: `example.com`\\n- Would match: `bexample.com` ❌ (WRONG!)\\n- Should only match: `.example.com`, `www.example.com` ✓\\n\\n**The Fix**:\\n```c\\nstatic bool tailmatch(const char *cooke_domain, const char *hostname)\\n{\\n  size_t cookie_domain_len = strlen(cooke_domain);\\n  size_t hostname_len = strlen(hostname);\\n  \\n  if(hostname_len < cookie_domain_len)\\n    return FALSE;\\n  \\n  if(!Curl_raw_equal(cooke_domain, hostname+hostname_len-cookie_domain_len))\\n    return FALSE;\\n  \\n  /* RFC6265 4.1.2.3: cookie domain must match exactly OR \\n     be preceded by a dot for subdomain matching */\\n  if(hostname_len == cookie_domain_len)\\n    return TRUE;  // Exact match\\n  if('.' == *(hostname + hostname_len - cookie_domain_len - 1))\\n    return TRUE;  // Proper subdomain with dot\\n  return FALSE;\\n}\\n```\\n\\n**Impact**: Cookies could leak across different domains, allowing unintended cookie sharing and potential security breaches.\\n\\n---\\n\\n### 3. **base64 encoding/decoding bounds checks in lib/base64.c**\\n\\n**CVE**: CVE-2016-8617 - [Commit efd24d5](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/efd24d57426bd77c9b5860e6b297904703750412) - \\\"base64: check for integer overflow on large input\\\" (September 27, 2016)\\n\\n**The Bug**:\\nOn 32-bit systems, very large input to base64 encoding could cause **integer overflow** when calculating the output buffer size.\\n\\n**Buggy Code**:\\n```c\\nstatic CURLcode base64_encode(const char *table64,\\n                              struct Curl_easy *data,\\n                              const char *inputbuff, size_t insize,\\n                              char **outptr, size_t *outlen)\\n{\\n  if(!insize)\\n    insize = strlen(indata);\\n  \\n  base64data = output = malloc(insize * 4 / 3 + 4); TRUE : FALSE;\n}\n```\n\n**What was wrong**: The function only checked if the cookie domain was a **suffix** of the hostname, but didn't verify there was a proper domain boundary (a dot). So:\n- Cookie domain: `example.com`\n- Would match: `bexample.com` ❌ (WRONG!)\n- Should only match: `.example.com`, `www.example.com` ✓\n\n**The Fix**:\n```c\nstatic bool tailmatch(const char *cooke_domain, const char *hostname)\n{\n  size_t cookie_domain_len = strlen(cooke_domain);\n  size_t hostname_len = strlen(hostname);\n  \n  if(hostname_len < cookie_domain_len)\n    return FALSE;\n  \n  if(!Curl_raw_equal(cooke_domain, hostname+hostname_len-cookie_domain_len))\n    return FALSE;\n  \n  /* RFC6265 4.1.2.3: cookie domain must match exactly OR \n     be preceded by a dot for subdomain matching */\n  if(hostname_len == cookie_domain_len)\n    return TRUE;  // Exact match\n  if('.' == *(hostname + hostname_len - cookie_domain_len - 1))\n    return TRUE;  // Proper subdomain with dot\n  return FALSE;\n}\n```\n\n**Impact**: Cookies could leak across different domains, allowing unintended cookie sharing and potential security breaches.\n\n---\n\n### 3. **base64 encoding/decoding bounds checks in lib/base64.c**\n\n**CVE**: CVE-2016-8617 - [Commit efd24d5](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/efd24d57426bd77c9b5860e6b297904703750412) - \"base64: check for integer overflow on large input\" (September 27, 2016)\n\n**The Bug**:\nOn 32-bit systems, very large input to base64 encoding could cause **integer overflow** when calculating the output buffer size.\n\n**Buggy Code**:\n```c\nstatic CURLcode base64_encode(const char *table64,\n                              struct Curl_easy *data,\n                              const char *inputbuff, size_t insize,\n                              char **outptr, size_t *outlen)\n{\n  if(!insize)\n    insize = strlen(indata);\n  \n  base64data = output = malloc(insize * 4 / 3 + 4);  // Overflow possible!\n  if(!output)\n    return CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n  // ...\n}\n```\n\n**What was wrong**: On 32-bit systems where `size_t` is 32 bits, if `insize` was very large (close to `UINT_MAX`), the calculation `insize * 4 / 3 + 4` could overflow, resulting in a small allocation. This would then lead to a **heap buffer overflow** when writing base64 data.\n\n**The Fix**:\n```c\nstatic CURLcode base64_encode(const char *table64, /*...*/)\n{\n  if(!insize)\n    insize = strlen(indata);\n  \n#if SIZEOF_SIZE_T == 4\n  if(insize > UINT_MAX/4)  // Bounds check to prevent overflow\n    return CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n#endif\n  \n  base64data = output = malloc(insize * 4 / 3 + 4);\n  if(!output)\n    return CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n  // ...\n}\n```\n\n**Impact**: Heap buffer overflow that could lead to crashes or arbitrary code execution on 32-bit systems with specially crafted large inputs.\n\n---\n\n### 4. **transfer shutdown in lib/transfer.c**\n\n[Commit 385c62a](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/385c62aabc388e62162c634e97ee61d1ab8bf81c) - \"lib: xfer_setup and non-blocking shutdown\" (June 10, 2024)\n\n**The Bug**:\nTransfer shutdown was previously **blocking**, which could cause the entire transfer to hang if the server didn't properly respond during SSL/TLS connection shutdown. This wasn't necessarily a security bug but a **robustness/denial-of-service issue**.\n\n**What was wrong**: \nThe old `Curl_conn_shutdown_blocking()` function would block indefinitely waiting for proper connection shutdown:\n\n```c\nCURLcode Curl_conn_shutdown_blocking(struct Curl_easy *data, int sockindex)\n{\n  // ... \n  while(cf) {\n    while(!done && !result) {\n      result = cf->cft->do_shutdown(cf, data, &done);\n      if(!result && !done) {\n        // Block waiting for socket to be ready\n        what = Curl_conn_cf_poll(cf, data, timeout_ms);\n        // Could hang here if server misbehaves\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  // ...\n}\n```\n\n**The Fix**:\nConverted shutdown to be **non-blocking** with proper state tracking:\n\n```c\nCURLcode Curl_conn_shutdown(struct Curl_easy *data, int sockindex, bool *done)\n{\n  // Non-blocking approach - return CURLE_OK with *done=FALSE if not finished\n  *done = FALSE;\n  \n  if(!Curl_shutdown_started(data, sockindex)) {\n    Curl_shutdown_start(data, sockindex, &now);\n  }\n  \n  while(cf) {\n    bool cfdone = FALSE;\n    result = cf->cft->do_shutdown(cf, data, &cfdone);\n    if(result)\n      return result;\n    else if(!cfdone) {\n      // Not done yet, return CURLE_OK and let caller retry later\n      return CURLE_OK;\n    }\n    cf = cf->next;\n  }\n  *done = (!result);\n  return result;\n}\n```\n\nThe code also added proper shutdown for **receiving** direction in `lib/transfer.c`:\n\n```c\nstatic CURLcode xfer_recv_shutdown(struct Curl_easy *data, bool *done)\n{\n  // Shutdown the receiving socket when transfer completes\n  int sockindex = (data->conn->sockfd == data->conn->sock[SECONDARYSOCKET]);\n  return Curl_conn_shutdown(data, sockindex, done);\n}\n```\n\n**Impact**: Prevented potential hangs/DoS when servers don't properly close SSL/TLS connections, improving transfer reliability especially for FTP over TLS.\n\n---\n\n## Summary\n\nAll four bugs demonstrate common security pitfalls:\n1. **NULL pointer dereference** - missing input validation\n2. **Cookie domain escape** - insufficient boundary checking allowing cross-domain leaks  \n3. **Integer overflow** - arithmetic overflow on 32-bit systems leading to heap overflow\n4. **Blocking operations** - potential DoS through connection shutdown hangs\n\nThe fixes added proper validation, bounds checking, and non-blocking state machine handling.\n\n## Sources\n\n- [type:commit (message:passwd_callback OR message:\"null pointer\" OR message:openssl.c) repo:github.com/curl/curl     struct Curl_easy *data,\n                              bool send_shutdown, bool *done)\n{\n  struct ssl_connect_data *connssl = cf->ctx;\n  struct ossl_ctx *octx = (struct ossl_ctx *)connssl->backend;\n  CURLcode result = CURLE_OK;\n  char buf[1024];\n  int nread = -1, err;\n  unsigned long sslerr;\n  size_t i;\n\n  DEBUGASSERT(octx);\n  if(!octx->ssl || cf->shutdown) {\n    *done = TRUE;\n    goto out;\n  }\n\n  connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_NONE;\n  *done = FALSE;\n  if(!(SSL_get_shutdown(octx->ssl) & SSL_SENT_SHUTDOWN)) {\n    /* We have not started the shutdown from our side yet. Check\n     * if the server already sent us one. */\n    ERR_clear_error();\n    for(i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {\n      nread = SSL_read(octx->ssl, buf, (int)sizeof(buf));\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown not sent, read -> %d\", nread);\n      if(nread <= 0)\n        break;\n    }\n    err = SSL_get_error(octx->ssl, nread);\n    if(!nread && err == SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN) {\n      bool input_pending;\n      /* Yes, it did. */\n      if(!send_shutdown) {\n        CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown received, not sending\");\n        *done = TRUE;\n        goto out;\n      }\n      else if(!cf->next->cft->is_alive(cf->next, data, &input_pending)) {\n        /* Server closed the connection after its closy notify. It\n         * seems not interested to see our close notify, so do not\n         * send it. We are done. */\n        connssl->peer_closed = TRUE;\n        CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"peer closed connection\");\n        *done = TRUE;\n        goto out;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  /* SSL should now have started the shutdown from our side. Since it\n   * was not complete, we are lacking the close notify from the server. */\n  if(send_shutdown && !(SSL_get_shutdown(octx->ssl) & SSL_SENT_SHUTDOWN)) {\n    ERR_clear_error();\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"send SSL close notify\");\n    if(SSL_shutdown(octx->ssl) == 1) {\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown finished\");\n      *done = TRUE;\n      goto out;\n    }\n    if(SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE == SSL_get_error(octx->ssl, nread)) {\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown still wants to send\");\n      connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_SEND;\n      goto out;\n    }\n    /* Having sent the close notify, we use SSL_read() to get the\n     * missing close notify from the server. */\n  }\n\n  for(i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {\n    ERR_clear_error();\n    nread = SSL_read(octx->ssl, buf, (int)sizeof(buf));\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown read -> %d\", nread);\n    if(nread <= 0)\n      break;\n  }\n  err = SSL_get_error(octx->ssl, nread);\n  switch(err) {\n  case SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN: /* no more data */\n    if(SSL_shutdown(octx->ssl) == 1)\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown finished\");\n    else\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown not received, but closed\");\n    *done = TRUE;\n    break;\n  case SSL_ERROR_NONE: /* just did not get anything */\n  case SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ:\n    /* SSL has send its notify and now wants to read the reply\n     * from the server. We are not really interested in that. */\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown sent, want receive\");\n    connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_RECV;\n    break;\n  case SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE:\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown send blocked\");\n    connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_SEND;\n    break;\n  default:\n    /* Server seems to have closed the connection without sending us\n     * a close notify. */\n    sslerr = ERR_get_error();\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown, ignore recv error: '%s', errno %d\",\n                (sslerr ?\n                 ossl_strerror(sslerr, buf, sizeof(buf)) :\n                 SSL_ERROR_to_str(err)),\n                SOCKERRNO);\n    *done = TRUE;\n    result = CURLE_OK;\n    break;\n  }\n\nout:\n  cf->shutdown = (result || *done);\n  return result;\n}\n\nstatic void ossl_close(struct Curl_cfilter *cf, struct Curl_easy *data)\n{\n  struct ssl_connect_data *connssl = cf->ctx;\n  struct ossl_ctx *octx = (struct ossl_ctx *)connssl->backend;\n\n  (void)data;\n  DEBUGASSERT(octx);\n\n  if(octx->ssl) {\n    SSL_free(octx->ssl);\n    octx->ssl = NULL;\n  }\n  if(octx->ssl_ctx) {\n    SSL_CTX_free(octx->ssl_ctx);\n    octx->ssl_ctx = NULL;\n    octx->x509_store_setup = FALSE;\n  }\n  if(octx->bio_method) {\n    ossl_bio_cf_method_free(octx->bio_method);\n    octx->bio_method = NULL;\n  }\n}\n\n/*\n * This function is called when the 'data' struct is going away. Otherwise, the (most specific) Common Name\n   field in the Subject field of the certificate MUST be used. Although\n   the use of the Common Name is existing practice, it is deprecated and\n   Certification Authorities are encouraged to use the dNSName instead.\n\n   Matching is performed using the matching rules specified by\n   [RFC2459]. If more than one identity of a given type is present in\n   the certificate (e.g., more than one dNSName name, a match in any one\n   of the set is considered acceptable.) Names may contain the wildcard\n   character * which is considered to match any single domain name\n   component or component fragment. E.g., *.a.com matches foo.a.com but\n   not bar.foo.a.com. f*.com matches foo.com but not bar.com.\n\n   In some cases, the URI is specified as an IP address rather than a\n   hostname. In this case, the iPAddress subjectAltName must be present\n   in the certificate and must exactly match the IP in the URI.\n\n   This function is now used from ngtcp2 (QUIC) as well.\n*/\nstatic CURLcode ossl_verifyhost(struct Curl_easy *data,\n                                struct connectdata *conn,\n                                struct ssl_peer *peer, X509 *server_cert)\n{\n  bool matched = FALSE;\n  int target; /* target type, GEN_DNS or GEN_IPADD */\n  size_t addrlen = 0;\n  STACK_OF(GENERAL_NAME) *altnames;\n#ifdef USE_IPV6\n  struct in6_addr addr;\n#else\n  struct in_addr peer->hostname, &addr))\n      return CURLE_PEER_FAILED_VERIFICATION;\n    target = GEN_IPADD;\n    addrlen = sizeof(struct in6_addr);\n    break;\n#endif\n  case CURL_SSL_PEER_DNS:\n    target = least\n       one, but we do not depend on it... */\n    numalts = sk_GENERAL_NAME_num(altnames);\n\n    /* loop through all alternatives - until a dnsmatch */\n    for(i = 0; (i < numalts) && !dnsmatched; i++) {\n      /* get a handle to alternative name number i */\n      const GENERAL_NAME *check = sk_GENERAL_NAME_value(altnames, i);\n\n      if(check->type == GEN_DNS)\n        dNSName = and length */\n        const char *altptr = (char *)ASN1_STRING_get0_data(check->d.ia5);\n        size_t altlen = (size_t) ASN1_STRING_length(check->d.ia5);\n\n        switch(target) {\n        case IA5String the data will be ASCII\"\n\n             It has been however verified that in 0.9.6 and 0.9.7, IA5String\n             is always null-terminated.\n          */\n          if(subj_alt_hostcheck(data, altptr, altlen,\n                                peer->hostname, hostlen,\n                                peer->dispname)) {\n            dnsmatched = TRUE;\n          }\n          break;\n\n        case GEN_IPADD: /* IP address comparison */\n          /* compare alternative IP address if the data chunk is the same size\n             our server IP address is */\n          if((altlen == addrlen) && !memcmp(altptr, &addr, altlen)) {\n            ipmatched = TRUE;\n            infof(data,\n                  \" subjectAltName: host \\\"%s\\\" matched cert's IP the last occurrence of a commonName in the\n       distinguished one to get the most significant one. */\n    int i = -1;\n    unsigned char *cn = NULL;\n    int cnlen = 0;\n    bool free_cn = X509_NAME_get_index_by_NID(name, NID_commonName, i)) >= 0)\n        i = j;\n    }\n\n    /* we have the name entry and we will now convert this to a string\n       that we can use for comparison. Doing this we support BMPstring,\n       UTF8, etc. */\n\n    if(i >= 0) {\n      ASN1_STRING *tmp =\n        X509_NAME_ENTRY_get_data(X509_NAME_get_entry(name, i));\n\n      /* In OpenSSL 0.9.7d and earlier, ASN1_STRING_to_UTF8 fails if the input\n         is already UTF-8 encoded. This code can be made\n         conditional in the future when OpenSSL has been fixed. */\n      if(tmp) {\n        if(ASN1_STRING_type(tmp) == V_ASN1_UTF8STRING) {\n          cnlen = free_cn = TRUE;\n        }\n\n        if((cnlen <= 0) || !cn)\n          result = CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n        else if((size_t)cnlen != strlen((char *)cn)) {\n          /* there was a terminating load_cacert_from_memory(X509_STORE *store,\n                                        const struct curl_blob *ca_info_blob)\n{\n  /* these need to be freed at the end */\n  BIO *cbio = NULL;\n  STACK_OF(X509_INFO) *inf = NULL;\n\n  /* everything else is just a reference */\n  int i, count = 0;\n  X509_INFO *itmp = NULL;\n\n  if(ca_info_blob->len > (size_t)INT_MAX)\n    return NULL);\n  if(!inf) {\n    BIO_free(cbio);\n    return CURLE_SSL_CACERT_BADFILE;\n  }\n\n  /* add each entry from PEM file to x509_store */\n  for(i = 0; i < (int)sk_X509_INFO_num(inf); ++i) {\n    itmp = sk_X509_INFO_value(inf, (ossl_valsize_t)i);\n    if(itmp->x509) {\n      if(X509_STORE_add_cert(store, itmp->x509)) {\n        ++count;\n      }\n      else {\n        /* set count to 0 to return an error */\n        count = 0;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n    if(itmp->crl) {\n      if(X509_STORE_add_crl(store, itmp->crl)) {\n        ++count;\n      }\n      else {\n        /* set count to 0 to return an error */\n        count = 0;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  sk_X509_INFO_pop_free(inf, X509_INFO_free);\n  BIO_free(cbio);\n\n  /* if we did not end up importing CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_RECV;\n      return CURLE_OK;\n    }\n    if(SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE == detail) {\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL_connect() -> want send\");\n      connssl->io_need = Curl_cfilter *cf,\n                                    struct Curl_easy *data,\n                                    bool nonblocking,\n                                    bool *done)\n{\n  CURLcode ossl_send(struct Curl_cfilter *cf,\n                         struct Curl_easy *data,\n                         const void *mem,\n                         size_t len,\n                         CURLcode *curlcode)\n{\n  /* SSL_write() is said to return 'int' while write() and send() returns\n     'size_t' */\n  int err;\n  char error_buffer[256];\n  sslerr_t sslerror;\n  int memlen;\n  int rc;\n  struct ssl_connect_data *connssl = cf->ctx;\n  struct ossl_ctx *octx = (struct ossl_ctx *)connssl->backend;\n\n  (void)data;\n  DEBUGASSERT(octx);\n\n  ERR_clear_error();\n\n  connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_NONE;\n  memlen = (len > (size_t)INT_MAX) ? *data)\n{\n  /* This might get called before it has been added to a multi handle */\n  if(data->multi && data->multi->ssl_seeded)\n    return CURLE_OK;\n\n  if(rand_enough()) {\n    /* OpenSSL 1.1.0+ (time_t)(i + 3)) << 8;\n      tv.tv_usec ^= (int) ((Curl_now().tv_sec + (time_t)Curl_now().tv_usec) *\n                           (time_t)(i + 4)) << 16;\n      memcpy(&randb[i * sizeof(struct RAND_LOAD_LENGTH);\n      if(rand_enough())\n        return CURLE_OK;\n    }\n  }\n\n  infof(data, \"libcurl is now using a weak random seed\");\n  return rand_enough() ? Since it\n   * was not complete, we are lacking the close notify from the server. */\n  if(send_shutdown && !(SSL_get_shutdown(octx->ssl) & SSL_SENT_SHUTDOWN)) {\n    ERR_clear_error();\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"send SSL close notify\");\n    if(SSL_shutdown(octx->ssl) == 1) {\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown finished\");\n      *done = TRUE;\n      goto out;\n    }\n    if(SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE == SSL_get_error(octx->ssl, nread)) {\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown still wants to send\");\n      connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_SEND;\n      goto out;\n    }\n    /* Having sent the close notify, we use SSL_read() to get the\n     * missing close notify from the server. */\n  }\n\n  for(i = 0; i < 10; ++i) {\n    ERR_clear_error();\n    nread = SSL_read(octx->ssl, buf, (int)sizeof(buf));\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown read -> %d\", nread);\n    if(nread <= 0)\n      break;\n  }\n  err = SSL_get_error(octx->ssl, nread);\n  switch(err) {\n  case SSL_ERROR_ZERO_RETURN: /* no more data */\n    if(SSL_shutdown(octx->ssl) == 1)\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown finished\");\n    else\n      CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown not received, but closed\");\n    *done = TRUE;\n    break;\n  case SSL_ERROR_NONE: /* just did not get anything */\n  case SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ:\n    /* SSL has send its notify and now wants to read the reply\n     * from the server. We are not really interested in that. */\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown sent, want receive\");\n    connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_RECV;\n    break;\n  case SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE:\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown send blocked\");\n    connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_SEND;\n    break;\n  default:\n    /* Server seems to have closed the connection without sending us\n     * a close notify. */\n    sslerr = ERR_get_error();\n    CURL_TRC_CF(data, cf, \"SSL shutdown, ignore recv error: '%s', errno %d\",\n                (sslerr ?\n                 ossl_strerror(sslerr, buf, sizeof(buf)) :\n                 SSL_ERROR_to_str(err)),\n                SOCKERRNO);\n    *done = TRUE;\n    result = CURLE_OK;\n    break;\n  }\n\nout:\n  cf->shutdown = (result || *done);\n  return result;\n}\n\nstatic void ossl_close(struct Curl_cfilter *cf, struct Curl_easy *data)\n{\n  struct ssl_connect_data *connssl = cf->ctx;\n  struct ossl_ctx *octx = (struct ossl_ctx *)connssl->backend;\n\n  (void)data;\n  DEBUGASSERT(octx);\n\n  if(octx->ssl) {\n    SSL_free(octx->ssl);\n    octx->ssl = NULL;\n  }\n  if(octx->ssl_ctx) {\n    SSL_CTX_free(octx->ssl_ctx);\n    octx->ssl_ctx = NULL;\n    octx->x509_store_setup = FALSE;\n  }\n  if(octx->bio_method) {\n    ossl_bio_cf_method_free(octx->bio_method);\n    octx->bio_method = NULL;\n  }\n}\n\n/*\n * This function is called when the 'data' struct is going away. Although\n   the use of the Common Name is existing practice, it is deprecated and\n   Certification Authorities are encouraged to use the dNSName instead.\n\n   Matching is performed using the matching rules specified by\n   [RFC2459]. But the interesting message-type\n     * is at 'buf[0]'.\n     */\n    if(ssl_ver == SSL3_VERSION_MAJOR && content_type)\n      tls_rt_name = tls_rt_type(content_type);\n    else\n      tls_rt_name = \"\";\n\n    if(content_type == SSL3_RT_CHANGE_CIPHER_SPEC) {\n      msg_type = *(char *)buf;\n      msg_name = \"Change cipher spec\";\n    }\n    else if(content_type == SSL3_RT_ALERT) {\n      msg_type = (((char *)buf)[0] << 8) + ((char *)buf)[1];\n      msg_name = SSL_alert_desc_string_long(msg_type);\n    }\n    else {\n      msg_type = *(char *)buf;\n      msg_name = ssl_msg_type(ssl_ver, msg_type);\n    }\n\n    txt_len = msnprintf(ssl_buf, sizeof(ssl_buf),\n                        \"%s (%s), %s, %s (%d):\\n\",\n                        verstr, direction ? \"OUT\" : \"IN\",\n                        tls_rt_name, msg_name, msg_type);\n    Curl_debug(data, CURLINFO_TEXT, ssl_buf, (size_t)txt_len);\n  }\n\n  Curl_debug(data, (direction == 1) ? CURLINFO_SSL_DATA_OUT :\n             CURLINFO_SSL_DATA_IN, (char *)buf, len);\n  (void) ssl;\n}\n#endif\n\n#ifdef USE_OPENSSL\n/* ====================================================== */\n\n/* Check for OpenSSL 1.0.2 which has ALPN support. */\n#undef HAS_ALPN\n#if OPENSSL_VERSION_NUMBER >= 0x10002000L       \\\n  && !defined(OPENSSL_NO_TLSEXT)\n#  define HAS_ALPN 1\n#endif\n\n#if load_cacert_from_memory(X509_STORE *store,\n                                        const struct curl_blob *ca_info_blob)\n{\n  /* these need to be freed at the end */\n  BIO *cbio = NULL;\n  STACK_OF(X509_INFO) *inf = NULL;\n\n  /* everything else is just a reference */\n  int i, count = 0;\n  X509_INFO *itmp = NULL;\n\n  if(ca_info_blob->len > (size_t)INT_MAX)\n    return CURLE_SSL_CACERT_BADFILE;\n\n  cbio = BIO_new_mem_buf(ca_info_blob->data, (int)ca_info_blob->len);\n  if(!cbio)\n    return CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n\n  inf = PEM_X509_INFO_read_bio(cbio, NULL, NULL, NULL);\n  if(!inf) {\n    BIO_free(cbio);\n    return CURLE_SSL_CACERT_BADFILE;\n  }\n\n  /* add each entry from PEM file to x509_store */\n  for(i = 0; i < (int)sk_X509_INFO_num(inf); ++i) {\n    itmp = sk_X509_INFO_value(inf, (ossl_valsize_t)i);\n    if(itmp->x509) {\n      if(X509_STORE_add_cert(store, itmp->x509)) {\n        ++count;\n      }\n      else {\n        /* set count to 0 to return an error */\n        count = 0;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n    if(itmp->crl) {\n      if(X509_STORE_add_crl(store, itmp->crl)) {\n        ++count;\n      }\n      else {\n        /* set count to 0 to return an error */\n        count = 0;\n        break;\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  sk_X509_INFO_pop_free(inf, X509_INFO_free);\n  BIO_free(cbio);\n\n  /* if we did not end up importing anything, treat that as an error */\n  return (count > 0) ? CURLE_OK : CURLE_SSL_CACERT_BADFILE;\n}\n\n#if defined(USE_WIN32_CRYPTO)\nstatic CURLcode import_windows_cert_store(struct Curl_easy *data,\n                                          const char *name,\n                                          X509_STORE *store,\n                                          bool *imported)\n{\n  CURLcode result = CURLE_OK;\n  HCERTSTORE hStore;\n\n  *imported = FALSE;\n\n  hStore = CertOpenSystemStoreA(0, name);\n  if(hStore) {\n    PCCERT_CONTEXT pContext = NULL;\n    /* The array of enhanced key usage OIDs will vary per certificate and\n       is declared outside of the loop so that rather than malloc/free each\n       iteration we can grow it with realloc, when necessary. */\n    CERT_ENHKEY_USAGE *enhkey_usage = NULL;\n    DWORD enhkey_usage_size = 0;\n\n    /* This loop makes a best effort to import all valid certificates from\n       the MS root store. If a certificate cannot be imported it is\n       skipped. 'result' is used to store only hard-fail conditions (such\n       as out of memory) that cause an early break. */\n    result = CURLE_OK;\n    for(;;) {\n      X509 *x509;\n      FILETIME now;\n      BYTE key_usage[2];\n      DWORD req_size;\n      const unsigned char *encoded_cert;\n      pContext = CertEnumCertificatesInStore(hStore, pContext);\n      if(!pContext)\n        break;\n\n#if defined(DEBUGBUILD) && !defined(CURL_DISABLE_VERBOSE_STRINGS)\n      else {\n        char cert_name[256];\n        if(!CertGetNameStringA(pContext, CERT_NAME_SIMPLE_DISPLAY_TYPE, 0,\n                               NULL, cert_name, sizeof(cert_name)))\n          infof(data, \"SSL: unknown cert name\");\n        else\n          infof(data, \"SSL: Checking cert \\\"%s\\\"\", cert_name);\n      }\n#endif\n      encoded_cert = (const unsigned char *)pContext->pbCertEncoded;\n      if(!encoded_cert)\n        continue;\n\n      GetSystemTimeAsFileTime(&now);\n      if(CompareFileTime(&pContext->pCertInfo->NotBefore, &now) > 0 ||\n         CompareFileTime(&now, &pContext->pCertInfo->NotAfter) > 0)\n        continue;\n\n      /* If key usage exists check for signing attribute */\n      if(CertGetIntendedKeyUsage(pContext->dwCertEncodingType,\n                                 pContext->pCertInfo,\n                                 key_usage, sizeof(key_usage))) {\n        if(!(key_usage[0] & CERT_KEY_CERT_SIGN_KEY_USAGE))\n          continue;\n      }\n      else if(GetLastError())\n        continue;\n\n      /* If enhanced key usage exists check for server auth attribute.\n       *\n       * Note \"In a Microsoft environment, a certificate might also have\n       * EKU extended properties that specify valid uses for the\n       * certificate.\"  The call below checks both, and behavior varies\n       * depending on what is found. For more details see\n       * CertGetEnhancedKeyUsage doc.\n       */\n      if(CertGetEnhancedKeyUsage(pContext, 0, NULL, &req_size)) {\n        if(req_size && req_size > enhkey_usage_size) {\n          void *tmp = realloc(enhkey_usage, req_size);\n\n          if(!tmp) {\n            failf(data, \"SSL: Out of memory allocating for OID list\");\n            result = CURLE_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n            break;\n          }\n\n          enhkey_usage = (CERT_ENHKEY_USAGE *)tmp;\n          enhkey_usage_size = req_size;\n        }\n\n        if(CertGetEnhancedKeyUsage(pContext, 0, enhkey_usage, &req_size)) {\n          if(!enhkey_usage->cUsageIdentifier) {\n            /* \"If GetLastError returns CRYPT_E_NOT_FOUND, the certificate\n               is good for all uses. If it returns zero, the certificate\n               has no valid uses.\" */\n            if((HRESULT)GetLastError() != CRYPT_E_NOT_FOUND)\n              continue;\n          }\n          else {\n            DWORD i;\n            bool found = FALSE;\n\n            for(i = 0; i < enhkey_usage->cUsageIdentifier; ++i) {\n              if(!strcmp(\"1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.1\" /* OID server auth */,\n                         enhkey_usage->rgpszUsageIdentifier[i])) {\n                found = TRUE;\n                break;\n              }\n            }\n\n            if(!found)\n              continue;\n          }\n        }\n        else\n          continue;\n      }\n      else\n        continue;\n\n      x509 = d2i_X509(NULL, &encoded_cert, (long)pContext->cbCertEncoded);\n      if(!x509)\n        continue;\n\n      /* Try to import the certificate. This may fail for legitimate\n         reasons such as duplicate certificate, which is allowed by MS but\n         not OpenSSL. */\n      if(X509_STORE_add_cert(store, x509) == 1) {\n#if defined(DEBUGBUILD) && !defined(CURL_DISABLE_VERBOSE_STRINGS)\n        infof(data, \"SSL: Imported cert\");\n#endif\n        *imported = TRUE;\n      }\n      X509_free(x509);\n    }\n\n    free(enhkey_usage);\n    CertFreeCertificateContext(pContext);\n    CertCloseStore(hStore, 0);\n\n    if(result)\n      return result;\n  }\n\n  return result;\n}\n#endif\n\nstatic CURLcode ossl_populate_x509_store(struct Curl_cfilter *cf,\n                                         struct Curl_easy *data,\n                                         X509_STORE *store)\n{\n  struct ssl_primary_config *conn_config = Curl_ssl_cf_get_primary_config(cf);\n  struct ssl_config_data *ssl_config = Curl_ssl_cf_get_config(cf, data);\n  CURLcode result = CURLE_OK;\n  X509_LOOKUP *lookup = NULL;\n  const struct curl_blob *ca_info_blob = conn_config->ca_info_blob;\n  const char * const ssl_cafile =\n    /* CURLOPT_CAINFO_BLOB overrides CURLOPT_CAINFO */\n    (ca_info_blob ? break; /* failed */\n\n    /* https://docs.openssl.org/master/man3/d2i_X509/ */\n    len2 = i2d_X509_PUBKEY(X509_get_X509_PUBKEY(cert), &temp);\n\n    /*\n     * These checks are verifying we got back ossl_send(struct Curl_cfilter *cf,\n                         struct Curl_easy *data,\n                         const void *mem,\n                         size_t len,\n                         CURLcode *curlcode)\n{\n  /* SSL_write() is said to return 'int' while write() and send() returns\n     'size_t' */\n  int err;\n  char error_buffer[256];\n  sslerr_t sslerror;\n  int memlen;\n  int rc;\n INT_MAX : (int)len;\n  rc = SSL_write(octx->ssl, mem, memlen);\n\n  if(rc <= 0) {\n    err = SSL_get_error(octx->ssl, rc);\n\n    switch(err) {\n    case SSL_ERROR_WANT_READ:\n      connssl->io_need = CURL_SSL_IO_NEED_RECV;\n      *curlcode = CURLE_AGAIN;\n      rc = -1;\n      goto out;\n    case SSL_ERROR_WANT_WRITE:\n      *curlcode = CURLE_AGAIN;\n      rc = -1;\n      goto out;\n    case SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL:\n    {\n      int sockerr = SOCKERRNO;\n\n      if(octx->io_result == CURLE_AGAIN) {\n        *curlcode = CURLE_AGAIN;\n        rc = -1;\n        goto out;\n      }\n      sslerror = ERR_get_error();\n      if(sslerror)\n        ossl_strerror(sslerror, error_buffer, sizeof(error_buffer));\n      else if(sockerr)\n        Curl_strerror(sockerr, error_buffer, sizeof(error_buffer));\n      else\n        msnprintf(error_buffer, sizeof(error_buffer), \"%s\",\n                  SSL_ERROR_to_str(err));\n\n      failf(data, OSSL_PACKAGE \" SSL_write: %s, errno %d\",\n            error_buffer, sockerr);\n      *curlcode = CURLE_SEND_ERROR;\n      rc = -1;\n      goto out;\n    }\n    case SSL_ERROR_SSL: {\n      /*  A failure in the SSL library occurred, usually a protocol error.\n          The OpenSSL error queue contains more information on the error. */\n      sslerror = ERR_get_error();\n      failf(data, \"SSL_write() error: %s\",\n            ossl_strerror(sslerror, error_buffer, sizeof(error_buffer)));\n      *curlcode = CURLE_SEND_ERROR;\n      rc = -1;\n      goto out;\n    }\n    default:\n      /* a true error */\n      failf(data, OSSL_PACKAGE \" SSL_write: %s, errno %d\",\n            SSL_ERROR_to_str(err), SOCKERRNO);\n      *curlcode = CURLE_SEND_ERROR;\n      rc = -1;\n      goto out;\n    }\n  }\n  *curlcode = CURLE_OK;\n\nout:\n  return (ssize_t)rc; To reduce risk, we require a\n         * dot OR the exact hostname being \"localhost\".\n         */\n        if(bad_domain(valuep, vlen))\n          domain = \":\";\n#endif\n\n        is_ip = Curl_host_is_ipnum(domain ? domain : valuep);\n\n        if(!domain\n           || (is_ip && !strncmp(valuep, domain, vlen) &&\n               (vlen == strlen(domain)))\n           || (!is_ip && cookie_tailmatch(valuep, vlen, domain))) {\n          strstore(&co->domain, valuep, vlen);\n          if(!co->domain)\n            return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n\n          if(!is_ip)\n            co->tailmatch = TRUE; /* we always do that if the domain name was\n                                     given */\n        }\n        else {\n          /*\n           * We did not get a tailmatch and then the attempted set domain is\n           * not a domain to which the current host belongs. Mark as bad.\n           */\n          infof(data, \"skipped cookie with bad tailmatch domain: %s\",\n                valuep);\n          return CERR_NO_TAILMATCH;\n        }\n      }\n      else if((nlen == 7) && strncasecompare(\"version\", namep, 7)) {\n        /* just ignore */\n      }\n      else if((nlen == 7) && strncasecompare(\"max-age\", namep, 7)) {\n        /*\n         * Defined in RFC2109:\n         *\n         * Optional. The Max-Age attribute defines the lifetime of the\n         * cookie, in seconds. The delta-seconds value is a decimal non-\n         * negative integer. After delta-seconds seconds elapse, the\n         * client should discard the cookie. A value of zero means the\n         * cookie should be discarded immediately.\n         */\n        CURLofft offt;\n        const char *maxage = valuep;\n        offt = curlx_strtoofft((*maxage == '\\\"') ?\n                               &maxage[1] : &maxage[0], NULL, 10,\n                               &co->expires);\n        switch(offt) {\n        case CURL_OFFT_FLOW:\n          /* overflow, used max value */\n          co->expires = CURL_OFF_T_MAX;\n          break;\n        case CURL_OFFT_INVAL:\n          /* negative or otherwise bad, expire */\n          co->expires = 1;\n          break;\n        case CURL_OFFT_OK:\n          if(!co->expires)\n            /* already expired */\n            co->expires = 1;\n          else if(CURL_OFF_T_MAX - now < co->expires)\n            /* would overflow */\n            co->expires = CURL_OFF_T_MAX;\n          else\n            co->expires += now;\n          break;\n        }\n        cap_expires(now, co);\n      }\n      else if((nlen == 7) && strncasecompare(\"expires\", namep, 7)) {\n        if(!co->expires && (vlen < MAX_DATE_LENGTH)) {\n          /*\n           * Let max-age have priority.\n           *\n           * If the date cannot get parsed for whatever reason, the cookie\n           * will be treated as a session cookie\n           */\n          char dbuf[MAX_DATE_LENGTH + 1];\n          memcpy(dbuf, valuep, vlen);\n          dbuf[vlen] = 0;\n          co->expires = Curl_getdate_capped(dbuf);\n\n          /*\n           * Session cookies have expires set to 0 so if we get that back\n           * from the date parser let's add a second to make it a\n           * non-session cookie\n           */\n          if(co->expires == 0)\n            co->expires = 1;\n          else if(co->expires < 0)\n            co->expires = 0;\n          cap_expires(now, co);\n        }\n      }\n\n      /*\n       * Else, this is the second (or more) name we do not know about!\n       */\n    }\n    else {\n      /* this is an \"illegal\" <what>=<this> pair */\n    }\n\n    while(*ptr && ISBLANK(*ptr))\n      ptr++;\n    if(*ptr == ';')\n      ptr++;\n    else\n      break;\n  } while(1);\n\n  if(!co->domain && domain) {\n    /* no domain was given in the header line, set the default */\n    co->domain = strdup(domain);\n    if(!co->domain)\n      return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n  }\n\n  if(!co->path && path) {\n    /*\n     * No path was given in the header line, set the default. Note that the\n     * passed-in path to this function MAY have a '?' and following part that\n     * MUST NOT be stored as part of the path.\n     */\n    char *queryp = strchr(path, '?');\n\n    /*\n     * queryp is where the interesting part of the path ends, so now we\n     * want to the find the last\n     */\n    char *endslash;\n    if(!queryp)\n      endslash = strrchr(path, '/');\n    else\n      endslash = memrchr(path, '/', (queryp - path));\n    if(endslash) {\n      size_t pathlen = (endslash-path + 1); /* include end slash */\n      co->path = Curl_memdup0(path, pathlen);\n      if(co->path) {\n        co->spath = sanitize_cookie_path(co->path);\n        if(!co->spath)\n          return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n      }\n      else\n        return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n    }\n  }\n\n  /*\n   * If we did not get a cookie name, or a bad one, the this is an illegal\n   * line so bail out.\n   */\n  if(!co->name)\n    return CERR_BAD;\n\n  data->req.setcookies++;\n  return CERR_OK;\n}\n\nstatic int\nparse_netscape(struct Cookie *co,\n               struct CookieInfo *ci,\n               const char *lineptr,\n               bool secure)  /* TRUE if connection is over secure\n                                origin */\n{\n  /*\n   * This line is NOT an HTTP header style line, we do offer support for\n   * reading the odd netscape cookies-file format here\n   */\n  const char *ptr, *next;\n  int fields;\n  size_t len;\n\n  /*\n   * In 2008, Internet Explorer introduced HTTP-only cookies to prevent XSS\n   * attacks. Cookies marked httpOnly are not accessible to JavaScript. In\n   * Firefox's cookie files, they are prefixed #HttpOnly_ and the rest\n   * remains as usual, so we skip 10 characters of the line.\n   */\n  if(strncmp(lineptr, \"#HttpOnly_\", 10) == 0) {\n    lineptr += 10;\n    co->httponly = TRUE;\n  }\n\n  if(lineptr[0]=='#')\n    /* do not even try the comments */\n    return CERR_COMMENT;\n\n  /*\n   * Now loop through the fields and init the struct we already have\n   * allocated\n   */\n  fields = 0;\n  for(next = lineptr; next; fields++) {\n    ptr = next;\n    len = strcspn(ptr, \"\\t\\r\\n\");\n    next = (ptr[len] == '\\t' ? &ptr[len + 1] : NULL);\n    switch(fields) {\n    case 0:\n      if(ptr[0]=='.') { /* skip preceding dots */\n        ptr++;\n        len--;\n      }\n      co->domain = Curl_memdup0(ptr, len);\n      if(!co->domain)\n        return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n      break;\n    case 1:\n      /*\n       * flag: A TRUE/FALSE value indicating if all machines within a given\n       * domain can access the variable. Set TRUE when the cookie says\n       * .domain.com and to false when the domain is complete www.domain.com\n       */\n      co->tailmatch = !!strncasecompare(ptr, \"TRUE\", len);\n      break;\n    case 2:\n      /* The file format allows the path field to remain not filled in */\n      if(strncmp(\"TRUE\", ptr, len) && strncmp(\"FALSE\", ptr, len)) {\n        /* only if the path does not look like a boolean option! */\n        co->path = Curl_memdup0(ptr, len);\n        if(!co->path)\n          return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n        else {\n          co->spath = sanitize_cookie_path(co->path);\n          if(!co->spath)\n            return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n        }\n        break;\n      }\n      /* this does not look like a path, make one up! */\n      co->path = strdup(\"/\");\n      if(!co->path)\n        return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n      co->spath = strdup(\"/\");\n      if(!co->spath)\n        return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n      fields++; /* add a field and fall down to secure */\n      FALLTHROUGH();\n    case 3:\n      co->secure = FALSE;\n      if(strncasecompare(ptr, \"TRUE\", len)) {\n        if(secure || ci->running)\n          co->secure = TRUE;\n        else\n          return CERR_BAD_SECURE;\n      }\n      break;\n    case 4:\n      {\n        char *endp;\n        const char *p;\n        /* make sure curlx_strtoofft won't read past the current field */\n        for(p = ptr; p < &ptr[len] && ISDIGIT(*p); ++p)\n          ;\n        if(p == ptr || p != &ptr[len] ||\n           curlx_strtoofft(ptr, &endp, 10, &co->expires) || endp != &ptr[len])\n          return CERR_RANGE;\n      }\n      break;\n    case 5:\n      co->name = Curl_memdup0(ptr, len);\n      if(!co->name)\n        return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n      else {\n        /* For Netscape file format cookies we check prefix on the name */\n        if(strncasecompare(\"__Secure-\", co->name, 9))\n          co->prefix_secure = TRUE;\n        else if(strncasecompare(\"__Host-\", co->name, 7))\n          co->prefix_host = TRUE;\n      }\n      break;\n    case 6:\n      co->value = Curl_memdup0(ptr, len);\n      if(!co->value)\n        return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n      break;\n    }\n  }\n  if(6 == fields) {\n    /* we got a cookie with blank contents, fix it */\n    co->value = strdup(\"\");\n    if(!co->value)\n      return CERR_OUT_OF_MEMORY;\n    else\n      fields++;\n  }\n\n  if(7 != fields)\n    /* we did not find the sufficient number of fields */\n    return CERR_FIELDS;\n\n  return CERR_OK;\n}\n\nstatic int\nis_public_suffix(struct Curl_easy *data,\n                 struct Cookie *co,\n                 const char *domain)\n{\n#ifdef USE_LIBPSL\n  /*\n   * Check if the domain is a Public Suffix and if yes, ignore the cookie. We\n   * must also check that the data handle is not NULL since the psl code will\n   * dereference it.\n   */\n  DEBUGF(infof(data, \"PSL check set-cookie '%s' for domain=%s in %s\",\n         co->name, co->domain, domain));\n  if(data && (domain && co->domain && !Curl_host_is_ipnum(co->domain))) {\n    bool acceptable = FALSE;\n    char lcase[256];\n    char lcookie[256];\n    size_t dlen = strlen(domain);\n    size_t clen = strlen(co->domain);\n    if((dlen < sizeof(lcase)) && (clen < sizeof(lcookie))) {\n      const psl_ctx_t *psl = Curl_psl_use(data);\n      if(psl) {\n        /* the PSL check requires lowercase domain name and pattern */\n        Curl_strntolower(lcase, domain, dlen + 1);\n        Curl_strntolower(lcookie, co->domain, clen + 1);\n        acceptable = psl_is_cookie_domain_acceptable(psl, lcase, lcookie);\n        Curl_psl_release(data);\n      }\n      else\n        infof(data, \"libpsl problem, rejecting cookie for satety\");\n    }\n\n    if(!acceptable) {\n      infof(data, \"cookie '%s' dropped, domain '%s' must not \"\n            \"set cookies for '%s'\", co->name, domain, co->domain);\n      return CERR_PSL;\n    }\n  }\n#else\n  (void)data;\n  (void)co;\n  (void)domain;\n  DEBUGF(infof(data, \"NO PSL to check set-cookie '%s' for domain=%s in %s\",\n         co->name, co->domain, domain));\n#endif\n  return CERR_OK;\n}\n\nstatic int\nreplace_existing(struct Curl_easy *data,\n                 struct Cookie *co,\n                 struct CookieInfo *ci,\n                 bool secure,\n                 bool *replacep)\n{\n  bool replace_old = FALSE;\n  struct Curl_llist_node *replace_n = NULL;\n  struct Curl_llist_node *n;\n  size_t myhash = cookiehash(co->domain);\n  for(n = Curl_llist_head(&ci->cookielist[myhash]); n; n = Curl_node_next(n)) {\n    struct Cookie *clist = Curl_node_elem(n);\n    if(!strcmp(clist->name, co->name)) {\n      /* the names are identical */\n      bool matching_domains = FALSE;\n\n      if(clist->domain && co->domain) {\n        if(strcasecompare(clist->domain, co->domain))\n          /* The domains are identical */\n          matching_domains = TRUE;\n      }\n      else if(!clist->domain && !co->domain)\n        matching_domains = TRUE;\n\n      if(matching_domains && /* the domains were identical */\n         clist->spath && co->spath && /* both have paths */\n         clist->secure && !co->secure && !secure) {\n        size_t cllen;\n        const char *sep;\n\n        /*\n         * A non-secure cookie may not overlay an existing secure cookie.\n         * For an existing cookie \"a\" with path \"/login\", refuse a new\n         * cookie \"a\" with for example path \"/login/en\", while the path\n         * \"/loginhelper\" is ok.\n         */\n\n        sep = strchr(clist->spath + 1, '/');\n\n        if(sep)\n          cllen = sep - clist->spath;\n        else\n          cllen = strlen(clist->spath);\n\n        if(strncasecompare(clist->spath, co->spath, cllen)) {\n          infof(data, \"cookie '%s' for domain '%s' dropped, would \"\n                \"overlay an existing cookie\", co->name, co->domain);\n          return CERR_BAD_SECURE;\n        }\n      }\n    }\n\n    if(!replace_n && !strcmp(clist->name, co->name)) {\n      /* the names are identical */\n\n      if(clist->domain && co->domain) {\n        if(strcasecompare(clist->domain, co->domain) &&\n          (clist->tailmatch == co->tailmatch))\n          /* The domains are identical */\n          replace_old = TRUE;\n      }\n      else if(!clist->domain && !co->domain)\n        replace_old = TRUE;\n\n      if(replace_old) {\n        /* the domains were identical */\n\n        if(clist->spath && co->spath &&\n           !strcasecompare(clist->spath, co->spath))\n          replace_old = FALSE;\n        else if(!clist->spath != !co->spath)\n          replace_old = FALSE;\n      }\n\n      if(replace_old && !co->livecookie && clist->livecookie) {\n        /*\n         * Both cookies matched fine, except that the already present cookie\n         * is \"live\", which means it was set from a header, while the new one\n         * was read from a file and thus is not \"live\". \"live\" cookies are\n         * preferred so the new cookie is freed.\n         */\n        return CERR_LIVE_WINS;\n      }\n      if(replace_old)\n        replace_n = n;\n    }\n  }\n  if(replace_n) {\n    struct Cookie *repl = Curl_node_elem(replace_n);\n\n    /* when replacing, creationtime is kept from old */\n    co->creationtime = repl->creationtime;\n\n    /* unlink the old */\n    Curl_node_remove(replace_n);\n\n    /* free the old cookie */\n    freecookie(repl);\n  }\n  *replacep = replace_old;\n  return CERR_OK;\n}\n\n/*\n * Curl_cookie_add\n *\n * Add a single cookie line to the cookie keeping object. Be aware that\n * sometimes we get an IP-only hostname, and that might also be a numerical\n * IPv6 address.\n *\n * Returns NULL on out of memory or invalid cookie. This is suboptimal,\n * as they should be treated separately.\n */\nstruct Cookie *\nCurl_cookie_add(struct Curl_easy *data,\n                struct CookieInfo *ci,\n                bool httpheader, /* TRUE if HTTP header-style line */\n                bool noexpire, /* if TRUE, skip remove_expired() */\n                const char *lineptr,   /* first character of the line */\n                const char *domain, /* default domain */\n                const char *path,   /* full path used when this cookie is set,\n                                       used to get default path for the cookie\n                                       unless set */\n                bool secure)  /* TRUE if connection is over secure origin */\n{\n  struct Cookie *co;\n  size_t myhash;\n  int rc;\n  bool replaces = FALSE;\n\n  DEBUGASSERT(data);\n  DEBUGASSERT(MAX_SET_COOKIE_AMOUNT <= 255); /* counter is an unsigned char */\n  if(data->req.setcookies >= MAX_SET_COOKIE_AMOUNT)\n    return NULL;\n\n  /* First, alloc and init a new struct for it */\n  co = calloc(1, sizeof(struct Cookie));\n  if(!co)\n    return NULL; /* bail out if we are this low on memory */\n\n  if(httpheader)\n    rc = parse_cookie_header(data, co, ci, lineptr, domain, path, secure);\n  else\n    rc = parse_netscape(co, ci, lineptr, secure);\n\n  if(rc)\n    goto fail;\n\n  if(co->prefix_secure && !co->secure)\n    /* The __Secure- prefix only requires that the cookie be set secure */\n    goto fail;\n\n  if(co->prefix_host) {\n    /*\n     * The __Host- prefix requires the cookie to be secure, have a \"/\" path\n     * and not have a domain set.\n     */\n    if(co->secure && co->path && strcmp(co->path, \"/\") == 0 && !co->tailmatch)\n      ;\n    else\n      goto fail;\n  }\n\n  if(!ci->running &&    /* read from a file */\n     ci->newsession &&  /* clean session cookies */\n     !co->expires)      /* this is a session cookie since it does not expire */\n    goto fail;\n\n  co->livecookie = ci->running;\n  co->creationtime = ++ci->lastct;\n\n  /*\n   * Now we have parsed the incoming line, we must now check if this supersedes\n   * an already existing cookie, which it may if the previous have the same\n   * domain and path as this.\n   */\n\n  /* remove expired cookies */\n  if(!noexpire)\n    remove_expired(ci);\n\n  if(is_public_suffix(data, co, domain))\n    goto fail;\n\n  if(replace_existing(data, co, ci, secure, &replaces))\n    goto fail;\n\n  /* add this cookie to the list */\n  myhash = cookiehash(co->domain);\n  Curl_llist_append(&ci->cookielist[myhash], co, &co->node);\n\n  if(ci->running)\n    /* Only show this when NOT reading the cookies from a file */\n    infof(data, \"%s cookie %s=\\\"%s\\\" for domain %s, path %s, \"\n          \"expire %\" FMT_OFF_T,\n          replaces ? \"Replaced\":\"Added\", co->name, co->value,\n          co->domain, co->path, co->expires);\n\n  if(!replaces)\n    ci->numcookies++; /* one more cookie in the jar */\n\n  /*\n   * Now that we have added a new cookie to the jar, update the expiration\n   * tracker in case it is the next one to expire.\n   */\n  if(co->expires && (co->expires < ci->next_expiration))\n    ci->next_expiration = co->expires;\n\n  return co;\nfail:\n  freecookie(co);\n  return NULL;\n}\n\n\n/*\n * Curl_cookie_init()\n *\n * Inits a cookie struct to read data from a local file. This is always\n * called before any cookies are set. File may be NULL in which case only the\n * struct is initialized. Is file is \"-\" then STDIN is read.\n *\n * If 'newsession' is TRUE, discard all \"session cookies\" on read from file.\n *\n * Note that 'data' might be called as NULL pointer. If data is NULL, 'file'\n * will be ignored.\n *\n * Returns NULL on out of memory. Invalid cookies are ignored.\n */\nstruct CookieInfo *Curl_cookie_init(struct Curl_easy *data,\n                                    const char *file,\n                                    struct CookieInfo *ci,\n                                    bool newsession)\n{\n  FILE *handle = NULL;\n\n  if(!ci) {\n    int i;\n\n    /* we did not get a struct, create one */\n    ci = calloc(1, sizeof(struct CookieInfo));\n    if(!ci)\n      return NULL; /* failed to get memory */\n\n    /* This does not use the destructor callback since we want to add\n       and remove to lists while keeping the cookie struct intact */\n    for(i = 0; i < COOKIE_HASH_SIZE; i++)\n      Curl_llist_init(&ci->cookielist[i], NULL);\n    /*\n     * Initialize the next_expiration time to signal that we do not have enough\n     * information yet.\n     */\n    ci->next_expiration = CURL_OFF_T_MAX;\n  }\n  ci->newsession = newsession; /* new session? */\n\n  if(data) {\n    FILE *fp = NULL;\n    if(file && *file) {\n      if(!strcmp(file, \"-\"))\n        fp = stdin;\n      else {\n        fp = fopen(file, \"rb\");\n        if(!fp)\n          infof(data, \"WARNING: failed to open cookie file \\\"%s\\\"\", file);\n        else\n          handle = fp;\n      }\n    }\n\n    ci->running = FALSE; /* this is not running, this is init */\n    if(fp) {\n      struct dynbuf buf;\n      Curl_dyn_init(&buf, MAX_COOKIE_LINE);\n      while(Curl_get_line(&buf, fp)) {\n        char *lineptr = Curl_dyn_ptr(&buf);\n        bool headerline = FALSE;\n        if(checkprefix(\"Set-Cookie:\", lineptr)) {\n          /* This is a cookie line, get it! */\n          lineptr += 11;\n          headerline = TRUE;\n          while(*lineptr && ISBLANK(*lineptr))\n            lineptr++;\n        }\n\n        Curl_cookie_add(data, ci, headerline, TRUE, lineptr, NULL, NULL, TRUE);\n      }\n      Curl_dyn_free(&buf); /* free the line buffer */\n\n      /*\n       * Remove expired cookies from the hash. We must make sure to run this\n       * after reading the file, and not on every cookie.\n       */\n      remove_expired(ci);\n\n      if(handle)\n        fclose(handle);\n    }\n    data->state.cookie_engine = TRUE;\n  }\n  ci->running = TRUE;          /* now, we are running */\n\n  return ci;\n}\n\n/*\n * cookie_sort\n *\n * Helper function to sort cookies such that the longest path gets before the\n * shorter path. Path, domain and name lengths are considered in that order,\n * with the creationtime as the tiebreaker. The creationtime is guaranteed to\n * be unique per cookie, so we know we will get an ordering at that point.\n */\nstatic int cookie_sort(const void *p1, const void *p2)\n{\n  struct Cookie *c1 = *(struct Cookie **)p1;\n  struct Cookie *c2 = *(struct Cookie **)p2;\n  size_t l1, l2;\n\n  /* 1 - compare cookie path lengths */\n  l1 = c1->path ? strlen(c1->path) : 0;\n  l2 = c2->path ? strlen(c2->path) : 0;\n\n  if(l1 != l2)\n    return (l2 > l1) ? 1 : -1; /* avoid size_t <=> int conversions */\n\n  /* 2 - compare cookie domain lengths */\n  l1 = c1->domain ? strlen(c1->domain) : 0;\n  l2 = c2->domain ? strlen(c2->domain) : 0;\n\n  if(l1 != l2)\n    return (l2 > l1) ? 1 : -1; /* avoid size_t <=> int conversions */\n\n  /* 3 - compare cookie name lengths */\n  l1 = c1->name ? strlen(c1->name) : 0;\n  l2 = c2->name ? strlen(c2->name) : 0;\n\n  if(l1 != l2)\n    return (l2 > l1) ? 1 : -1;\n\n  /* 4 - compare cookie creation time */\n  return (c2->creationtime > c1->creationtime) ? 1 : -1;\n}\n\n/*\n * cookie_sort_ct\n *\n * Helper function to sort cookies according to creation time.\n */\nstatic int cookie_sort_ct(const void *p1, const void *p2)\n{\n  struct Cookie *c1 = *(struct Cookie **)p1;\n  struct Cookie *c2 = *(struct Cookie **)p2;\n\n  return (c2->creationtime > c1->creationtime) ? 1 : -1;\n}\n\n/*\n * Curl_cookie_getlist\n *\n * For a given host and path, return a linked list of cookies that the client\n * should send to the server if used now. The secure boolean informs the cookie\n * if a secure connection is achieved or not.\n *\n * It shall only return cookies that have not expired.\n *\n * Returns 0 when there is a list returned. Otherwise non-zero.\n */\nint Curl_cookie_getlist(struct Curl_easy *data,\n                        struct CookieInfo *ci,\n                        const char *host, const char *path,\n                        bool secure,\n                        struct Curl_llist *list)\n{\n  size_t matches = 0;\n  bool is_ip;\n  const size_t myhash = cookiehash(host);\n  struct Curl_llist_node *n;\n\n  Curl_llist_init(list, NULL);\n\n  if(!ci || !Curl_llist_count(&ci->cookielist[myhash]))\n    return 1; /* no cookie struct or no cookies in the struct */\n\n  /* at first, remove expired cookies */\n  remove_expired(ci);\n\n  /* check if host is an IP(v4|v6) address */\n  is_ip = Curl_host_is_ipnum(host);\n\n  for(n = Curl_llist_head(&ci->cookielist[myhash]);\n      n; n = Curl_node_next(n)) {\n    struct Cookie *co = Curl_node_elem(n);\n\n    /* if the cookie requires we are secure we must only continue if we are! */\n    if(co->secure ? secure : TRUE) {\n\n      /* now check if the domain is correct */\n      if(!co->domain ||\n         (co->tailmatch && !is_ip &&\n          cookie_tailmatch(co->domain, strlen(co->domain), host)) ||\n         ((!co->tailmatch || is_ip) && strcasecompare(host, co->domain)) ) {\n        /*\n         * the right part of the host matches the domain stuff in the\n         * cookie data\n         */\n\n        /*\n         * now check the left part of the path with the cookies path\n         * requirement\n         */\n        if(!co->spath || pathmatch(co->spath, path) ) {\n\n          /*\n           * This is a match and we add it to the return-linked-list\n           */\n          Curl_llist_append(list, co, &co->getnode);\n          matches++;\n          if(matches >= MAX_COOKIE_SEND_AMOUNT) {\n            infof(data, \"Included max number of cookies (%zu) in request!\",\n                  matches);\n            break;\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  }\n\n  if(matches) {\n    /*\n     * Now we need to make sure that if there is a name appearing more than\n     * once, the longest specified path version comes first.
